headline: Rhode Island federal judge vacates EPA shutdown of Solar for All grants
dek: The ruling clears the way for the $7 billion clean-energy program to resume, including a $49.3 million allocation intended for Rhode Island.
body: A Rhode Island federal judge has ruled that the Environmental Protection Agency acted unlawfully when it terminated the Solar for All grant program, setting aside the agency’s decision and sending the nationwide initiative back into legal effect.

U.S. District Judge Mary S. McElroy issued the decision Friday in a case brought by the Rhode Island AFL-CIO, Rhode Island Center for Justice, solar businesses and other plaintiffs. The program was created under the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act to expand solar access and lower energy costs for low- and moderate-income households.

The court said Congress intended the EPA to keep administering grants that had already been obligated and that the agency lacked statutory authority to end the program. Rhode Island had been allocated $49.3 million through the state Office of Energy Resources, but the money had been left in limbo after the EPA’s August 2025 termination.

The ruling does not set out a timetable for restarting the grants or specify whether existing recipients can proceed without new applications. The EPA said it was reviewing the decision and considering an appeal, while Rhode Island officials said they need clarity from the federal government before moving ahead with the state’s allocation.
author: NorthEast News Desk
